strings.name: James Cameron
strings.summary: James Cameron moved from low-budget genre filmmaking to large productions, combining storytelling and screen technology in The Terminator, Titanic and Avatar. With production teams, he advanced digital characters, stereoscopic filming and underwater performance capture. He also pursued deep-sea exploration. His influence connects commercial cinema with technical practice, beyond box-office rankings.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to 2026. This is not a complete catalogue of works or appearances; later plans are not treated as completed events.
strings.influence.rationale: Titanic and Avatar combined commercial storytelling with image technology, influencing digital effects and stereoscopic filmmaking.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Attended Fullerton College in the United States; did not complete a degree
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Applying film technology
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Worked with teams to use digital effects, stereoscopic photography and performance capture in large-scale narrative films.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Solo descent to the deep ocean
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Piloted DEEPSEA CHALLENGER to Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench in 2012.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Lifetime artistic achievement award
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Canada’s Governor General’s Performing Arts Awards honored his film career.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Avatar: Fire and Ash released
strings.timeline.event-2.text: The third Avatar film he directed opened in the United States.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Avatar: The Way of Water released
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Continued the Pandora story using underwater performance capture.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Reached Challenger Deep
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Completed a solo descent in a submersible developed by the expedition team.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Avatar released
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Combined digital characters and stereoscopic images, advancing commercial 3D cinema.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Titanic won Academy Awards
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Personally received Oscars for directing, best picture and film editing.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Titanic released
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Combined historical disaster, romance and large-scale effects production.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Terminator 2 released
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Developed computer-generated characters and visual effects with his team.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Aliens released
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Directed an action-oriented sequel to an established science-fiction film.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Breakthrough with The Terminator
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Wrote and directed the science-fiction action film that established his reputation.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Moved to California
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Moved from Canada with his family and later attended Fullerton College.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Ontario
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born and raised in Canada before building a film career in the United States.
